newsitem.title: USA: DKNY deal disappoints Designer investors.
newsitem.headline: DKNY deal disappoints Designer investors.

text.p: Designer Holdings Ltd shares slumped on Monday after its $60 million, 30-year pact to license Donna Karan International Inc's DKNY jeanswear disappointed investors.
The company's shares dropped 2-1/2, or almost 10 percent, to 24-1/4.
The stock led the losing stocks on the New York Stock Exchange on a percent basis. It went public in May, swelling to 25-3/8 from its offering price of $18.

"People were expecting the deal to be accretive this year and they did not expect that Designer Holdings would have to pay so much," said Manish Shah, editor of the IPO Maven, who has been tracking the stock.

Designer Holdings said the deal would not add to its earnings until the second half of 1997. It said it would make an initial payment of $6 million and would pay an additional $54 million over the next four years.
Shah said the pact was widely expected by investors to come sooner, based on the company's roadshow, management meetings, and reports in industry publications.
Designer Holdings, which also said will fund "an extensive advertising campaign" to launch the new line, was not immediately available to comment.
